item.title: Hakeem Jeffries moves closer to becoming first Black US House speaker
item.description: The New York Democrat secured 251 votes in favour and 11 against, but faces pressure from progressive lawmakers demanding commitments on healthcare, immigration and other key issues.

item.title: Euronews Verify: Can the EU close Russia's sanctions loopholes?
item.description: Another batch of EU sanctions targeting Russian banks, oil refineries and Russia's "shadow fleet" is expected later this month. But are sanctions actually effective against Moscow?

item.title: Former Macron ally Philippe unveils conservative agenda as French centre and right loses ground
item.description: Socialist, centrist and conservative candidates have been struggling to gain ground ahead of France's presidential elections, amid a race dominated by the hard left and far-right.

item.title: French broadcaster faces backlash after revealing feminist guest's marriage live on air
item.description: An activist criticised a French public broadcaster after a presenter revealed her marriage to a senior TV executive, sparking controversy over transparency rules and political reactions.

item.title: No heating or AC needed in France's first housing of its kind
item.description: French real estate company Nexity presented the first apartment building of its kind on Tuesday, which is designed to maintain an interior temperature between 20 °C and 26 °C without heating or air conditioning.

item.title: Europe Tonight: EU proposes €45bn Ukraine loan as Trump, Xi and Putin meet
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen unveils a new joint-debt package for Kyiv, an unprecedented US-China-Russia trilateral summit unfolds at APEC, industry figures warn Europe cannot sleep through the AI revolution, and IEA chief Fatih Birol urges a faster shift to electricity.

item.title: Designing Qatar’s new creative economy, from innovation hubs to incubation spaces
item.description: Creativity is becoming part of Qatar’s economic vision. Beyond galleries and exhibition spaces, Qatar is investing in infrastructures designed to nurture creatives so that their concepts can turn into creation.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 18th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 18th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: EPP ready to suspend Vučić’s SNS party in December
item.description: The party leadership will submit the proposal to the political assembly, where it is expected to secure approval. SNS could make a comeback, provided it meets certain conditions.

item.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis off US highways after California ban
item.description: Regulators called the robotaxis an "imminent hazard" after one tried to overtake police cars and three others drove into a live roadworks zone, just as the company prepares to expand into Europe.

item.title: Storms Bruna and Charles bring record rain and winds to Portugal and Madeira
item.description: The two storms combined meant that several records for maximum wind gusts and rainfall were broken in the first 12 days of November, according to the Portuguese Institute for the Sea and the Atmosphere (IPMA).

item.title: Israeli military launches new operation on central Gaza despite ceasefire
item.description: The military says it is targeting Hamas infrastructure near two refugee camps, while Hamas has accused Israel of violating the truce in place since October 2025.

item.title: EU has failed to curb harmful 'forever chemicals', auditors warn
item.description: EU auditors warn that slow regulation, patchy enforcement and outdated food and drinking water safety limits are leaving Europeans exposed to harmful chemicals, six years after Brussels pledged to phase out their non-essential uses.

item.title: The Dardenne Brothers: 'We need to ensure that there remains a sense of humanity in cinema'
item.description: Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne will receive the European Lifetime Achievement Award from the European Film Academy, in recognition of their body of work. Euronews Culture sat down with the filmmaking duo to discuss the prize, the perils of AI, and the evolution of European cinema.

item.title: New footage showing damage to key bridge linking Crimea to Russia
item.description: New footage shared by a Ukrainian Telegram channel appears to show extensive damage to the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea to mainland Russia.

item.title: Amazon pledges €6.3bn for renewable energy projects in India: Who will benefit from the clean electricity?
item.description: Some of the electricity generated will be used to power the company's data centres.

item.title: Robots serve ice cream and coffee in China's tech hub
item.description: In Shenzhen, China, humanoid robots serve coffee and ice cream while AI developers use human-recorded movements to train machines for everyday jobs.

item.title: UK government fights back over bacon crisps and marmalade claims
item.description: From smoky-flavoured snacks to ketchup sachets, ministers are pushing back against claims that closer ties with Brussels will mean a new wave of EU rules for British consumers.

item.title: GTA 6 countdown begins as billboards go up from Tokyo to Sydney
item.description: GTA VI fever grips Australia, Japan and New Zealand ahead of its 19 November release, with record downloads expected.

item.title: Singer Julio Iglesias under investigation for alleged sexual offences
item.description: The Spanish National High Court has admitted a complaint filed by two former employees of Julio Iglesias alleging sexual offences, bodily harm and degrading treatment. The singer has been summoned to testify on 3 February.

item.title: Iraqi court jails six French Islamic State members for life
item.description: More than 5,700 Islamic State detainees whom the US moved from Syria to Iraq are due to go on trial from Sunday, while rights groups question whether Iraq’s courts are fair.

item.title: Baku, Tbilisi and Astana join forces to expand Middle Corridor as Belgian firms eye investment
item.description: Azerbaijan, Georgia and Kazakhstan have drawn up a joint plan to increase Middle Corridor freight capacity to around 30 million tonnes a year by 2029, as Belgian companies discuss a logistics hub in Kazakhstan and digital upgrades to the Asia-Europe trade route.

item.title: Meet the Kazakh artist who campaigns against nuclear weapons
item.description: Born without arms near the Semipalatinsk nuclear test site, Karipbek Kuyukov became an artist and anti-nuclear activist. Today, he continues to campaign against nuclear weapons through his art and public appearances.

item.title: Iraq pumps oil to Turkey again after 12 years to bypass Hormuz disruption
item.description: The line, which can carry up to 750,000 barrels a day, was shut in 2014 after attacks by the so-called Islamic State terrorist group, and Iraq and Turkey agreed in August on a one-year arrangement for shipments while talks on a longer deal continue.

item.title: Hungarian ethno-punk bands join forces for Brussels dance-floor show
item.description: Hungary’s Besh o droM and Bohemian Betyars will perform together for the first time in Brussels on Friday, at the request of the Balkan Trafik festival. Besh o droM founder Gergely Barcza promises a big party and says Central European and Balkan cultures are moving closer together.

item.title: Consumer screening tests make baseless health claims, UK study finds
item.description: Easy access to dubious health tests should be considered a “patient safety issue,” researchers said.

item.title: Canada and China expand tariff relief on pork, seafood and metals amid US trade tensions
item.description: US tariffs have put pressure on Canadian exporters and pushed Ottawa to seek new markets. Canada is rebuilding trade ties with China while continuing talks with Washington to protect its car industry and other businesses that depend on the US market.

item.title: Trump and Putin shake hands in first encounter since 2025
item.description: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are preparing for historic three-way talks in China, bringing the three leaders together in person for the first time.

item.title: Opening a small business takes 18 times as long in Germany as in France, study finds
item.description: Setting up a small business in Germany takes almost 4,000 hours of red tape, the equivalent of nearly 500 eight-hour working days. That is the longest among 27 countries across Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and nearly 18 times as long as in France, which ranked first in a new study.

item.title: Estado Novo interpretive centre opens in Salazar's birthplace in Santa Comba Dão
item.description: The Estado Novo Interpretive Centre occupies a former primary school in the town where the Portuguese dictator was born and is dedicated to studying the regime and resistance movements.

item.title: Fossil fuel exit becomes COP31 flashpoint – but four more European countries are taking the leap
item.description: Four more EU countries have joined Finland, France, Germany and the Netherlands in publishing national roadmaps for the transition away from fossil fuels.

item.title: From the steppe to the global stage: Mongolia’s COP17 legacy
item.description: Mongolia hosts UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar, showcasing its capacity, spotlighting rangelands and securing billion-dollar pledges for land restoration.

item.title: Europe cannot 'sleep through the AI revolution': Tech leaders urge EU to take action
item.description: Tech leaders, including Yann LeCun, Nobel laureate Philippe Aghion and the CEOs of ElevenLabs and Lovable, call on the EU to secure a dedicated AI allocation in its 2028-2034 budget.

item.title: Police in Bangladesh clash with garment workers demanding higher minimum wages
item.description: Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 takas (€215), up from 12,500 takas (€89) and say rising living costs have eroded their purchasing power.

item.title: Zelenskyy proposes 10 more humanitarian evacuations after Oleshky
item.description: Zelenskyy did not name the 10 settlements and said Ukraine’s delegation would raise the plan with US mediators, while Putin has separately suggested a similar operation in Kostiantynivka, which Ukraine says Russia does not control.

item.title: Trump and Putin shake hands ahead of high-stakes trilateral summit in China
item.description: China’s Xi welcomed his US and Russian counterparts at the APEC summit as the three global powers’ leaders gear up for their first trilateral meeting. Trump shook hands with Putin, expressing hope about the chances of ending the war in Ukraine.

item.title: UK inflation rises to 3.6% as petrol and diesel prices climb
item.description: Higher fuel prices pushed UK inflation up from 3.5% in September to 3.6% in October. Diesel hit a record high, while prices for food and non-alcoholic drinks rose at their slowest pace in five years.

item.title: EU-UK summit: Leaked draft reveals ambition and limits of Brexit reset
item.description: A decade after the Brexit referendum, Brussels and London are poised to deepen ties on trade, defence and energy, but draft summit conclusions seen by Euronews reveal lingering political divisions.

item.title: Marco Rubio says no evidence recent tech outages in US are linked or 'nefarious'
item.description: Air travel was disrupted because of what the Trump administration called outdated equipment, causing regulators to halt all flights from taking off for several hours on Friday evening.

item.title: Mexico owns the only non-Chinese panda in the world: President Sheinbaum asks Xi Jinping for a mate
item.description: Claudia Sheinbaum met Chinese president Xi Jinping at the APEC summit.

item.title: Voyager 1 now 25.9 billion km from Earth, still active nearly 50 years after leaving our planet
item.description: It set off at a time when mobile phones were still science fiction. Nearly half a century later, Voyager 1 continues its journey through space.

item.title: Iran’s army chief vows ‘more crushing’ response if US attacks again
item.description: Army commander-in-chief Amir Hatami said Iranian forces would strike the US “along with its supporters” wherever they were based, as CENTCOM confirmed the USS Theodore Roosevelt had joined two other carriers in the region.

item.title: Catnomics: global cat market exceeds €100bn and drives pet economy
item.description: Worldwide, more and more families are choosing to adopt a cat, and the global market for food, gadgets and merchandising is worth over one hundred billion euros, driving the pet economy.

item.title: AI finds security flaw in Java, world’s third-largest programming language
item.description: The company that found the PHP flaw in October has used AI to uncover another security flaw in the widely used Java programming language.

item.title: Peru releases seven pelicans rescued from El Niño's effects
item.description: Seven rehabilitated pelicans return to the wild in Peru as the country opens its first state-run marine wildlife centre to protect seabirds affected by El Niño.

item.title: Trump ordered to give sworn testimony in BBC defamation case by January
item.description: The broadcaster says the US president has been avoiding its lawyers, and both sides have been told to be ready for trial in May.

item.title: Hacked fridges show the cost of 'vintage' infrastructure, and AI makes it worse, says Cisco executive
item.description: The real cyber threat is ageing infrastructure as well as AI, a Cisco executive tells Euronews Next.

item.title: ECB draws parallels between AI boom and dotcom bubble as tech giants pile on debt
item.description: The European Central Bank drew parallels between the AI boom and the dotcom bubble in its Financial Stability Review on Wednesday, warning that a wave of large IPOs could signal late-cycle exuberance as tech giants pile on debt, leaving markets exposed to an abrupt sell-off.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 18th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 18th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Nearly 300,000 children abroad receive German benefits, sparking political backlash
item.description: New figures show that children of Polish nationals account for the largest share of Germany’s child benefit payments abroad, fuelling calls from some politicians to restrict payments to families living outside the country.
